audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Akshan levels 1-3 and Skill everywhere after, while Ziggs holds a 58.33% win rate — the packet itself flags the contradiction.
audit.why: The mirror audit raised the same contradiction and deliberately did NOT flip the chart, so flipping it from this side would put the two pages into disagreement without a decision from the user. Re-raised as a question instead.
audit.corrected: No side or rating edits proposed; the prose was corrected in place so the early-game claim at least matches the kit.

audit.whatIsWrong: The 3-5 spike credits Going Rogue with move speed that lets him dodge Bouncing Bomb, and no cooldown numbers anchor any spike.
audit.why: Going Rogue (W) grants camouflage, and its move speed and mana regen apply while moving toward a Scoundrel — an enemy who has killed one of his allies. In a normal laning phase there is no Scoundrel, so that speed is not a laning dodge tool. What actually carries his early game is Avengerang (Q, 9/8/7/6/5s) plus the every-third-hit Dirty Fighting shield.
audit.corrected: spikes[0].text rebuilt on the 850 range, the wave-extension, the shield and his 7s Q; whys[2] rebuilt on Heroic Swing needing terrain.

audit.whatIsWrong: The founding claim 'your Q out-ranges' is false, wants.foe[1] treats E grapple and Heroic Swing as two abilities, and Going Rogue's camouflage is never mentioned despite Ziggs having no reveal in his kit.
audit.why: Bouncing Bomb and Avengerang are both 850, and Avengerang extends its range through every enemy it clips, so across a wave his reaches further. What Ziggs genuinely wins is tempo: Q every 6s at rank 1 against his 9s, with Short Fuse's cooldown pulled forward by every ability cast. Heroic Swing (E) is one ability and it needs terrain to hook — he is also knocked off it on collision with champions or terrain.
audit.corrected: tldr and whys[0] restated on tempo rather than range; wants.foe[1] corrected to one ability off a wall; dontsFull[2].d now carries the Control Ward / sweeper requirement against Going Rogue.

edits.before: A real poke war — your Q out-ranges, his Heroic Swing punishes. Trade bombs and dodge the answer.
edits.after: Both Qs reach 850 — you win tempo, not range: yours is 6s to his 9s. Bomb, step back, repeat.

edits.before: Level 1 Akshan out-trades you with Q and passive shields.
edits.after: Level 1 Avengerang plus Dirty Fighting shields out-trade you.

edits.before: Level 3 W speed and E grapple let him dodge your bombs and win trades.
edits.after: Level 3 Heroic Swing needs terrain — deny the walls and his poke stalls.

edits.before: Akshan bullies you here: his Q Avengerang plus passive Dirty Fighting shields out-trade your poke, and his W grants him movement speed to dodge Bouncing Bomb.
edits.after: Akshan bullies you here: Avengerang matches your 850 and extends through the wave, and Dirty Fighting shields him every third hit — trade while his 7s Q is down.

edits.before: Use E grapple and Heroic Swing to dodge your poke and close distance
edits.after: Use Heroic Swing off a wall to dodge your poke and close distance

edits.before: His swing engage/escape — fight only while it is down. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Short Fuse plus a 6s Q out-tempos his 9s Avengerang — every cast pulls your empowered auto forward.

edits.before: Burning W Satchel for damage and then standing in Heroic Swing range with no escape — the only way this lane kills you.
edits.after: Going Rogue camouflages him and Ziggs has no reveal — a Control Ward and a sweeper are the only way you see the flank coming at you.
